links.label: Managed cloud MLOps platform
links.description: Adopt a fully managed cloud platform spanning substantial portions of model development and operations.
links.reason: The passage discusses assembling MLOps from multiple tools, including cloud-compatible services like SageMaker, but advocates a custom-built ecosystem rather than adopting a fully managed cloud MLOps platform.

links.label: User-defined dataset validation
links.description: Custom routines detect inconsistencies, incorrect associations, missing values, and other data errors.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes user-defined validation routines that detect inconsistent associations, incorrect postal codes, missing values, and other dataset errors.

links.label: Dedicated feature engineering pipeline
links.description: A distinct pipeline selects, transforms, combines, and prepares raw data before algorithm use.
links.reason: The passage describes a distinct data engineering pipeline that cleans and transforms raw data into datasets for algorithms, but it does not explicitly describe feature selection, combination, or feature-specific engineering.

links.label: Three-way prediction input contract
links.description: Supply predictions with model artifacts, processed data, and fresh live signals.
links.reason: The passage explicitly defines algorithms as handling three input types—models, previously processed data, and fresh live signals—matching the stated prediction input contract.

links.label: Schema-anomaly pipeline halt
links.description: Stop training or processing when incoming features are unexpected, missing, or invalid.
links.reason: The passage supports automatic schema/domain validation of incoming data but does not state that processing or training halts when anomalies are found.

links.label: Automated retraining-and-deployment pipeline
links.description: Pipeline automation that retrains, validates, and deploys models from offline development.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes an ML pipeline that automates retraining and deployment of new models, with CI/CD automating testing and deployment.

links.label: Neural architecture search
links.description: Automated search selects neural architectures using defined spaces, metrics, and search algorithms.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes NAS as automated selection among architectures using defined search spaces, evaluation metrics, and search algorithms.

links.label: Batch and real-time processing support
links.description: Accommodate both batch and real-time execution modes in the ML processing architecture.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that a production-ready ML system should support both batch and real-time processing.

links.label: Offline batch training
links.description: Training runs as an offline process rather than during prediction requests.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes offline batch computation as a process that periodically precomputes results, contrasting it with online computation during requests.

links.label: Notebook-based prototyping
links.description: Data scientists prototype with notebooks despite an enterprise-provided platform.
links.reason: The passage explicitly discusses using Jupyter notebooks for data exploration and experimentation, while recommending moving to a proper project for larger-scale work.

links.label: Centralized consistent storage
links.description: Accessible data is retained in a consistent structure, ideally in one centralized location.
links.reason: The passage explicitly recommends storing accessible data in a consistent structure and conveniently in one place, directly describing centralized consistent storage.

links.label: Multi-language implementation support
links.description: Use infrastructure that permits services or ML components to be implemented in multiple programming languages.
links.reason: The passage explicitly supports allowing data scientists to use code without being forced to port it to R, implying infrastructure that accommodates implementations in different programming languages.

links.label: Containerized prediction microservice
links.description: A prediction model is packaged and deployed as a containerized microservice.
links.reason: The passage mentions support for containers and microservices but does not clearly describe packaging and deploying a prediction model as a containerized microservice.

links.label: Automated ML lifecycle management
links.description: Automate training, deployment, retraining, and related lifecycle operations to reduce manual effort.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes automating the ML lifecycle, including training, deployment, retraining, continuous delivery, monitoring, and validation, to reduce manual effort and speed production.

links.label: Microservice architecture
links.description: Clearly separated product components are independently served as microservices.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes using a microservice architecture, including separate services that independently monitor streams, analyze data, and manage model serving.

links.label: Single-objective error minimization
links.description: Considering one error objective instead of broader operational criteria was rejected for model assessment.
links.reason: The passage explicitly rejects relying solely on error minimization, emphasizing broader criteria such as stability, ethics, fairness, explainability, user experience, and edge-case performance for model assessment.

links.label: Local-machine data access
links.description: Develop by accessing protected data directly from a local machine.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that local-machine data access was prohibited and describes using secure VMs instead, clearly rejecting this option.

links.label: Software-metrics-only monitoring
links.description: Rely exclusively on software metrics to monitor a production model.
links.reason: The passage explicitly rejects relying only on software metrics, directly supporting the stated rejection of software-metrics-only monitoring.

links.label: Direct underlying-data access
links.description: Allowing direct access to underlying data was explicitly rejected as an infrastructure access approach.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that organizations do not want too many users to have direct access to the underlying data, indicating that this access approach was rejected.

links.label: Business-KPI-only monitoring
links.description: Wait exclusively for downstream product or business KPIs to monitor model behavior.
links.reason: The passage explicitly rejects waiting only for downstream business KPIs by stating that doing so is too late and that machine-learning monitoring requires distinct practices.

links.label: Active model performance monitoring
links.description: The source explicitly rejected active model-performance monitoring as the selected monitoring approach.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that level 0 lacks active performance monitoring, describing an approach that does not track predictions or detect performance degradation.

links.label: Avoided repeated notebook computation
links.description: Avoid repeated expensive training, retrieval, or database computation through cached results.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes Jupyter caching cell results to avoid repeating expensive ML training, data downloads, and database queries.

links.label: Improved transformation code quality
links.description: A structured development environment improves the quality of transformation code.
links.reason: The passage discusses data pipelines, data quality, and their fragility, but does not describe a structured development environment improving transformation code quality.

links.label: Managed platform flexibility and scalability
links.description: Flexibility and scalability resulting from using a fully managed platform.
links.reason: The passage identifies SageMaker as a fully managed end-to-end ML platform, directly supporting the option and its associated flexibility and scalability benefits.

links.label: Production accuracy requirement
links.description: Require AutoML-produced models to meet the accuracy needed for real-world use.
links.reason: The passage explicitly evaluates candidate models by accuracy and validates that the selected model performs adequately before deployment.

links.label: Partial monitoring coverage
links.description: Only a minority of deployed models receive monitoring, leaving substantial operational blind spots.
links.reason: The passage states there is no active performance monitoring, but it does not indicate that only a minority of deployed models are monitored or quantify partial coverage.

links.label: Model degradation
links.description: Changing real-world data causes predictive performance to decline over time.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that changing live data causes model degradation, meaning predictive performance decreases over time.

links.label: Duplicated notebook queries
links.description: Repeated notebook query cells create duplicated query code.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that using notebook cell magic for similar queries leads data scientists to create duplicate cells and duplicate query code.

links.label: Data-type mismatch detection
links.description: Observed validation output identifying inputs whose types violate dataset expectations.
links.reason: The passage explicitly reports a Model Monitor datatype_check violation, identifying inputs that fail expected data-type validation.

links.label: Replicable IDE code development
links.description: Use an IDE setup that supports proper, repeatable code and results.
links.reason: The passage supports reproducible code development through identical dev/prod dependencies and technical stacks, but it does not specifically describe or adopt an IDE setup.

links.label: Notebook showcasing and exploratory workflow
links.description: Use interactive notebooks for presenting results and conducting exploratory data analysis.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes notebooks as interactive, sharable environments combining code, text, plots, and data analysis, directly supporting their use for exploratory and results-presenting workflows.
